title: Sorting-bound external-memory breadth-first search
formal: Can exact single-source unweighted distances in every undirected graph be computed in O(S(n+m)) external-memory I/Os, even when M<n?
definitions: Use the single-disk external-memory model with an internal store of M records and transfer blocks of B consecutive records, for all integers B≥1,M≥2B. One I/O reads or writes one block; all input reads, preprocessing transfers and output writes count. Records have a constant number of fields; vertex identifiers and pointers have O(log(n+m+2)) bits. Records and numeric fields are indivisible: no packing arbitrarily many labels or weights into one field, and no decoding such packed information by arithmetic. Internal comparison, copying, address calculation and permitted numeric arithmetic on resident fields are free, but internal storage remains M records. Use at most (n+m)^{O(1)} external records and a uniform deterministic algorithm knowing M,B. Let N=n+m and S(N)=max{1,N/B}·max{1,log_{M/B}(max{1,N/B})}; the max conventions include small inputs. The bound sought is O(S(N)) I/Os with an absolute constant for every permitted M,B, including M<n. Input is a contiguous vertex list and an arbitrarily ordered edge list for a simple undirected graph on [n], plus source s. Output is one record per vertex with its distance from s, using +∞ for unreachable vertices; no explicit list of every shortest path is required. Every edge has length one. Distances are integers in {0,…,n−1} or +∞, fitting one numeric field. Temporary numeric values and indices have O(log(n+m+2)) bits. The input may be disconnected and output records may be in any order provided every vertex is identified.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of all stated guarantees, or prove the precise target impossible. State any complexity hypothesis used in a conditional impossibility.
context: The source improves external BFS beyond straightforward vertex-by-vertex access but still has an additional term beyond sorting. Semi-external bounds assume the vertex set fits in memory.
why: This asks whether graph traversal can match the basic external-memory sorting bound.

import_provenance.original_statement: Can exact breadth-first distances in an arbitrary undirected graph with n vertices and m edges be computed in O(Sort(n+m)) I/Os, even when its vertex set does not fit in RAM? Here Sort(N)=Θ((N/B)·max{1,log_(M/B)(N/B)}) is the external sorting bound, with memory M and block size B in the standard indivisible-record I/O model.
